plans.title: Heart Failure
plans.summary: Decreased cardiac output and fluid overload in chronic heart failure.

diagnoses.related: related to altered myocardial contractility and increased preload/afterload
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by dyspnea, fatigue, crackles, an S3 heart sound, and reduced activity tolerance
subjective: Reports shortness of breath with exertion
States “I feel exhausted all the time.”
outcomes: Client maintains adequate cardiac output as evidenced by clear lungs, SpO₂ >94%, and stable vital signs.
Client tolerates activity without excessive dyspnea by discharge.

interventions.i: Monitor vital signs, heart rhythm, and oxygen saturation.
Weigh the client daily at the same time.
interventions.r: A 2–3 lb gain in a day signals fluid retention.

interventions.i: Administer diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta-blockers as prescribed.
Position in semi- to high-Fowler's.
interventions.r: Eases breathing and reduces venous return to the heart.

interventions.i: Provide rest periods between activities.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client maintained SpO₂ >94% with clear lung sounds and stable weight; tolerated ambulation without severe dyspnea.

diagnoses.related: related to compromised regulatory mechanisms (reduced renal perfusion activating RAAS)
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by edema, rapid weight gain, crackles, and jugular venous distention
subjective: Reports swelling in the legs and rings feeling tight
outcomes: Client achieves balanced intake and output and returns toward baseline weight.

interventions.i: Monitor strict intake and output.
interventions.r: Quantifies fluid balance and diuretic effectiveness.

interventions.i: Restrict sodium and fluids as ordered.
interventions.r: Reduces fluid retention and cardiac workload.

interventions.i: Monitor electrolytes, especially potassium.
Elevate edematous extremities.
interventions.r: Promotes venous return and reduces swelling.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client's intake and output balanced; weight decreased 2 kg; edema reduced to trace.

plans.title: Pneumonia
plans.summary: Airway clearance and gas exchange problems from pulmonary infection.

diagnoses.related: related to excessive tracheobronchial secretions and inflammation
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by a productive cough, adventitious lung sounds, and dyspnea
subjective: Reports a cough with thick yellow sputum
outcomes: Client maintains a patent airway with clear or clearing breath sounds and effective cough.

interventions.i: Encourage coughing and deep breathing; use incentive spirometry.
Increase fluid intake unless contraindicated.
Position in semi-Fowler's and reposition frequently.
Administer antibiotics and expectorants as prescribed.
Suction as needed.
interventions.r: Clears secretions the client cannot expel.

diagnoses.evaluation: Breath sounds clearing; client demonstrates an effective cough and expectorates secretions.

diagnoses.related: related to alveolar-capillary membrane changes from infection
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by hypoxemia, dyspnea, and altered ABGs
outcomes: Client maintains SpO₂ ≥94% and shows no signs of hypoxia.

interventions.i: Monitor SpO₂ and ABGs.
interventions.r: Tracks oxygenation and the response to therapy.

interventions.i: Administer oxygen as prescribed.
Assess level of consciousness.
interventions.r: Restlessness/confusion is an early sign of hypoxia.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client maintained SpO₂ ≥94% and remained alert and oriented.

plans.title: Diabetes Mellitus
plans.summary: Glucose stability and self-management education for diabetes.

diagnoses.related: related to insufficient insulin, dietary intake, and knowledge deficit
subjective: States uncertainty about how to adjust insulin
outcomes: Client maintains blood glucose within the prescribed target range.

interventions.i: Monitor blood glucose as ordered.
interventions.r: Guides insulin dosing and detects highs/lows.

interventions.i: Administer insulin/oral agents as prescribed.
Teach signs of hypo- and hyperglycemia and the Rule of 15.
Reinforce consistent carbohydrate intake and activity.
Teach sick-day management.
interventions.r: Illness raises glucose and insulin needs.

diagnoses.evaluation: Blood glucose trended into target range; client verbalized signs of hypo/hyperglycemia.

diagnoses.related: related to a new diagnosis and unfamiliarity with self-care
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by questions and inaccurate return demonstration
subjective: Asks how to give an injection
States “I don’t know what I can eat.”
outcomes: Client correctly demonstrates glucose monitoring and insulin administration before discharge.

interventions.i: Teach and have the client demonstrate glucose monitoring and insulin injection.
Teach foot care and daily inspection.
Review when to call the provider.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client demonstrated correct technique and verbalized foot-care and follow-up instructions.

plans.title: COPD
plans.summary: Gas exchange and activity tolerance in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

diagnoses.related: related to airflow limitation and air trapping
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by dyspnea, abnormal ABGs, and decreased SpO₂
outcomes: Client maintains SpO₂ within the individualized target (often 88–92%).

interventions.i: Administer oxygen to the prescribed target (often 88–92%).
interventions.r: Corrects hypoxemia without blunting the hypoxic drive.

interventions.i: Teach pursed-lip breathing and tripod positioning.
interventions.r: Prolongs expiration and reduces air trapping.

interventions.i: Administer bronchodilators/inhaled steroids as prescribed.
Support smoking cessation.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client maintained SpO₂ 88–92% and used pursed-lip breathing effectively.

diagnoses.related: related to an imbalance between oxygen supply and demand
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by exertional dyspnea and fatigue
subjective: Reports needing to rest after walking a short distance
outcomes: Client performs ADLs with decreased dyspnea using energy-conservation techniques.

interventions.i: Pace activities with rest periods.
Teach energy-conservation techniques.
Encourage pulmonary rehabilitation.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client completed ADLs with rest periods and reduced dyspnea.

plans.title: Acute Pain (Post-op)
plans.summary: Managing acute surgical pain safely and effectively.

diagnoses.related: related to tissue trauma from a surgical incision
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by a pain report of 8/10, guarding, grimacing, and elevated heart rate and blood pressure
outcomes: Client reports pain ≤3/10 and participates in recovery activities without respiratory depression.

interventions.i: Assess pain (location, quality, intensity) regularly with a scale.
interventions.r: Pain is subjective; consistent assessment guides treatment.

interventions.i: Administer analgesics before pain becomes severe.
interventions.r: Preventing peaks controls pain with lower doses.

interventions.i: Assess respiratory rate before giving opioids; hold if <12.
Use nonpharmacologic measures (positioning, ice, distraction).
Initiate a bowel regimen with opioids.
Reassess pain after intervention.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client rated pain ≤3/10, ambulated as ordered, and maintained a respiratory rate ≥12.

plans.title: Risk for Falls
plans.summary: Preventing falls in a high-risk hospitalized client.

diagnoses.related: related to advanced age, impaired mobility, and medications causing orthostasis/sedation
outcomes: Client remains free of falls throughout hospitalization.

interventions.i: Complete a fall-risk assessment and flag the client.
Keep the bed in the lowest position with the call light in reach.
interventions.r: Reduces injury and the need to get up alone.

interventions.i: Provide non-skid footwear and a clear, uncluttered path.
Offer scheduled toileting.
interventions.r: Reduces urgent, unassisted trips to the bathroom.

interventions.i: Assist with ambulation and change positions slowly.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client remained free of falls; used the call light for assistance.

diagnoses.related: related to prolonged pressure over a bony prominence and immobility
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by a stage 2 sacral pressure injury
subjective: Reports being unable to reposition independently
objective: Stage 2 sacral ulcer with a pink wound bed
outcomes: Client's pressure injury shows evidence of healing with no new areas of breakdown.

interventions.i: Reposition at least every 2 hours.
Use a pressure-redistribution surface.
Keep skin clean and dry; manage moisture.
Assess skin and stage the wound each shift.
Optimize nutrition and protein/fluid intake.

diagnoses.evaluation: Wound bed showed granulation with no new breakdown; skin remained intact elsewhere.

plans.title: Infection / Sepsis Risk
plans.summary: Preventing and recognizing infection in an at-risk client.

diagnoses.related: related to invasive lines, surgical wounds, and compromised defenses
subjective: States understanding of the importance of hand hygiene
outcomes: Client remains free of infection as evidenced by normothermia and a normal white blood cell count.

interventions.i: Perform hand hygiene and use aseptic technique for all invasive care.
interventions.r: The single most effective way to prevent infection.

interventions.i: Monitor temperature, WBC, and the appearance of lines/wounds.
Obtain cultures before starting antibiotics, then give antibiotics on time.
interventions.r: Preserves culture accuracy and treats promptly.

interventions.i: Assess for early sepsis (fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, confusion, rising lactate).
Teach the client signs of infection to report.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client remained afebrile with a normal WBC and no signs of local or systemic infection.
